# claims v1

## Who may do what

For each action, the combinations `sekisho check` walked, put together where Cedar answers them alike and the same policies decide. Rows that differ in one column only are one row, the column holding their values: `any` is every value the column takes, `not …` every value but one. `-` is a column that does not apply to the row (the roles of a workflow, say).

### action `pay_claim`

Pay a claim

- It guards `openapi "api/desk.json" operation payClaim`.
- Principals: `User`, `Workflow`. Resources: `Claim`, the id read from the operation's argument `claimId`.
- Computed: `payer` (under Computed values below).
- 6 combinations, 3 of them allowed.

#### Allowed

| principal | adjuster | workflow | payer | Deciding policies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| User | yes | - | any | adjusters_pay_claims |
| Workflow | - | pay | desk | the_workflow_pays_the_desks_claims |

#### Denied

- No permit applies to the 3 combinations that are denied.

<details>
<summary>The 2 rows that deny</summary>

| principal | adjuster | workflow | payer | Deciding policies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| User | no | - | any | no permit applies |
| Workflow | - | pay | person | no permit applies |

</details>

## Policies

Each policy as the `.gate` writes it, beside the Cedar `sekisho gen --target cedar` generates for it. A permit allows the combinations it applies to; a forbid denies those it applies to, and wins where a permit applies too. Cedar denies a combination no policy applies to. A condition on a rule's answer names the value as the `.rule` writes it (`desk`) in the `.gate`, and as the string Cedar is given (`"desk"`) in the Cedar.

### permit `adjusters_pay_claims`

An adjuster pays any claim

- On `pay_claim`, it allows 2 combinations, and no other permit allows any of them.

`claims.gate`

```gate
permit adjusters_pay_claims
  description "An adjuster pays any claim"
  principal in adjuster
  action pay_claim
```

`cedar/claims.cedar`

```cedar
@id("claims/adjusters_pay_claims")
@doc("An adjuster pays any claim")
permit (
  principal in Claims::Role::"adjuster",
  action == Claims::Action::"pay_claim",
  resource is Claims::Claim
);
```

### permit `the_workflow_pays_the_desks_claims`

The workflow pays the claims the rule leaves to the desk

- On `pay_claim`, it allows 1 combination, which no other permit allows.

`claims.gate`

```gate
permit the_workflow_pays_the_desks_claims
  description "The workflow pays the claims the rule leaves to the desk"
  principal is workflow pay
  action pay_claim
  when payer is desk
```

`cedar/claims.cedar`

```cedar
@id("claims/the_workflow_pays_the_desks_claims")
@doc("The workflow pays the claims the rule leaves to the desk")
permit (
  principal == Claims::Workflow::"pay",
  action == Claims::Action::"pay_claim",
  resource is Claims::Claim
)
when { context.payer == "desk" };
```

## Computed values

What an action computes and gives Cedar in its context. The generated code computes each one from the service's own data, the operation's arguments and the server's clock, and never takes it from the caller. The pages of the rules and the dates are the pages for people that rulec and koyomi draw, as they draw them.

### `payer` of `pay_claim`

- Written: `payer = who_pays(amount: resource.amount).who`
- Computed by `rulec "rules/who_pays.rule" output who`, from `resource.amount`.
- Its values: `desk` and `person`; Cedar is given the strings `"desk"` and `"person"`.

## Roles

- `adjuster`: Pays the claims the desk does not. Its `can` lists `pay_claim`.

Whether a principal holding one role alone (and the roles it includes) is allowed each action: always, in every combination of the rest; sometimes, allowed in some combinations and denied in others; never, denied in every one. `-` is an action that does not take the principal's type. Where a role writes `can`, `sekisho check` holds the actions it is always or sometimes allowed to it.

| principal | `pay_claim` |
|---|---|
| `User` holding `adjuster` | always |

## Workflows

A workflow calls the operations as itself: in Cedar, the principal `Workflow::"<name>"`. For each workflow, the actions it is allowed, and how far.

### workflow `pay`

Pays a claim the rule leaves to the desk, and hands the others to a person

- Its flow: `dandori "flows/pay.flow"`.

| action | Allowed |
|---|---|
| `pay_claim` | sometimes (1 of 2 combinations allowed) |

#### What the gate says the flow holds of a resource

The `resource` lines under the workflow. Where the flow gives the value as the id of the resource, the gate says each attribute of the resource is the value of the flow beside it. `ritsu check` rests on these lines when it asks whether the gate allows the calls of the flow.

| Line | resource | The flow's value that is its id | Attribute | The flow's value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | `Claim` | `claim_id` | `amount` | `amount` |

> [!NOTE]
> These lines are an assumption whoever wrote the gate makes. Nothing checks that the resource the service reads holds what the flow holds. That each value of the flow is one its attribute takes is checked by `ritsu sekisho check` (E212).

#### What the flow calls

Each operation a task of the flow calls, the action that guards it, and whether the workflow is allowed that action at the call: over the combinations the runs that reach the call can come to (what the call gives, and what the arms of each `match` on the way leave). It is what `ritsu check` holds across the languages.

| Line | Task | Operation | Guarded by | Allowed | Error on a denial |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | `pay_claim` | `openapi "api/desk.json" operation payClaim` | `pay_claim` | always (given the gate's `resource` lines) | `denied` |

What the runs that reach a call hold there:

- Line 30: `who_pays(amount: resource.amount).who` (the flow's `r.who`) is `desk`.

> [!NOTE]
> An answer marked "given the gate's `resource` lines" is the answer where the resource the service reads holds what the `resource` lines under the workflow say the flow holds. Nothing checks that it does.
